decision: The repository is created as a skeleton whose module contracts throw, rather than as a working slice of any epic.
rationale: The P0 design pack states that P0 implementation waits for BT-G0 and a Work Package with explicit, expiring authority. BT-G0 is unrecorded. A skeleton that tests its own boundaries is buildable without that authority; a contract with behaviour behind it is not. Every exported function therefore throws with a message naming the epic that would fill it.
alternatives: Implement the tenancy module far enough to be useful, and mark it provisional. Rejected: it would create the very claim AGENTS.md section 12 forbids.
Create only directories and READMEs with no code. Rejected: the boundary rules could then not be observed firing, so the repository would carry an untested instrument.
authority: operator instruction to build the repository from the guide, 2026-09-08

decision: The seven dependency rules are generated from modules/modules.yaml into .dependency-cruiser.cjs, and a hand edit of the generated file fails the build.
rationale: The P0.2 design makes the registry, not the checker, the source of the rules, so that swapping the checker is cheap and a module outside the registry cannot import or be imported. The generator has a --check mode that compares the generated files against what the registry would produce now; that comparison is the generation step of negative control 7.
alternatives: Hand-write the dependency-cruiser config. Rejected: the registry would then describe the modules while the config decided them, and the two would drift.
Use eslint-plugin-boundaries instead. Deferred: ADR-001 chooses the checker; the rules are generated, so the switch stays cheap.

decision: The registry reader is a purpose-built strict parser for the registry shape, not a general YAML library.
rationale: It keeps scripts/ dependency-free, which is the pattern the P0.2 design names for the migration lint, and it lets the reader refuse a shape rather than silently accept one. A silent accept of a malformed registry would generate a rule set that protects nothing, which is the failure mode worth spending strictness on. It throws with a line number on any deviation.
alternatives: Add a YAML dependency. Rejected for now: the registry has one fixed shape and the reader must run before install in CI if that ordering is ever wanted.
Store the registry as JSON. Rejected: the file is read by humans deciding module boundaries, and it carries substantial commentary.
authority: P0.2 design, open question 5, the deterministic-script pattern

decision: Ten of the twelve negative controls of the P0.2 design are observed firing on deliberate fixtures; control 6 and every runtime control are recorded as declared non-coverage rather than passed.
rationale: Control 6 is a push straight to main and a merge with a failing check. Its refusal is the evidence, and only a repository administrator can create the protection that produces it, so an agent claiming it would be claiming a human decision. The runtime half of each control needs a running service and a database, and nothing runs. Recording them as non-coverage keeps the evidence honest; recording them as passed would make the whole matrix worthless.
alternatives: Omit the uncoverable controls from the records entirely. Rejected: a gap that reads as an omission rather than a decision is what the Architect stage rule forbids.
authority: AGENTS.md section 9, declared coverage and declared non-coverage

decision: The brokerage module named for the broker policy representation is registered as policy-record, not policy.
rationale: The migration lint refuses a P0 table named for the four domain words the security proof lists, one of which is policy, and ARCH-001 is emphatic that a broker policy representation is not the insurer-authoritative issued contract. The longer name keeps that distinction in the registry itself rather than only in prose, and keeps the module name from reading as the insurer record.
alternatives: Register it as policy and allow-list it in the lint. Rejected: an allow-list on the first row weakens the rule before it has ever fired.
authority: ARCH-001 section 9, data ownership; P0.SECURITY-PROOF control 6
